subject: Re: RFI — Log continuity, exportability and delivery SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@federatedbank.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: legal@federatedbank.com
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI — Log continuity, exportability and delivery SLA clarifications

Nikhil,

Thanks for taking this request. Federated is preparing an RFP response and we need concrete answers about Redwood's logging/audit export capabilities for regulatory evidence. High level asks below — please respond with the canonical answer and any samples or playbooks you can share.

1) Which artifacts are captured by default for hosted customers? (API request/response, model inputs, model outputs, system events, auth events, KV/prefix cache traces?)
2) Retention windows you support out-of-the-box and options for longer retention (legal hold / enterprise export).
3) Export formats and delivery mechanisms (NDJSON/Parquet/CSV, S3 presigned link, direct SFTP, on-prem handoff).
4) Tamper-evidence and chain-of-custody (hashing, signed manifests, time-stamping).
5) Redaction or PII suppression options prior to export and guidance on reproducibility for investigations.
6) SLA for a full forensic export (end-to-end time to deliver a complete archive for a 90-day window).

Can you also attach a sample manifest and an example export file stub? Federated would like to understand what they would receive and the expected metadata fields (timestamps, request_id, model_version, route, tokens, truncated flags, etc.). We are hoping for answers by end of week — ideally within 48 hours.

Appreciate it — we may loop in procurement afterwards.

Best,
Brian
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Federated Bank

---

(Attachment requested: sample manifest)

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@federatedbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-21T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI — Log continuity, exportability and delivery SLA clarifications

Brian — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, source-of-truth style response and I've attached our export playbook + a sample manifest CSV. If you want, we can convert the sample into Parquet for size benchmarking.

1) Default captured artifacts (hosted API):
   - API gateway request/response metadata (timestamp, client IP, request_id, route, status_code)
   - Model input tokens (truncated by default after X tokens for retention policy), prompt/trace pointer for reproductions
   - Model output tokens and finalOutput (tokenized representation + reconstructed text)
   - Auth events: token issuance/refresh, key-id, actor id
   - Serving runtime events: model_version, backend_host, batch_id, kv_cache_miss/hit markers
   - System warnings/errors and rate-limit events

2) Retention defaults and extended options:
   - Hosted default: 90 days for full-text model inputs/outputs; 365 days for auth and audit indexes (indexes are smaller, searchable).
   - Dedicated/Private customers: configurable retention up to customer policy — we support immutable snapshots for legal hold.
   - For regulatory holds we provide a preservation mode where records are written to an immutable S3 bucket with object-lock (WORM) and a signed manifest.

3) Export formats & delivery mechanisms:
   - Supported formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) as the default forensic bundle; optional Parquet for columnar analytics; CSV manifest for index summary.
   - Delivery options: presigned S3 (time-limited), SFTP (enterprise customers), Azure Blob SAS, or physical encrypted disk for on-prem handoffs if required.
   - Each bundle includes: compressed (gzip) file set, export_manifest.csv, sha256_manifest.txt, and delivery_metadata.json (timestamps + job id).

4) Tamper-evidence & chain-of-custody:
   - Every export run produces a sha256 checksum for each file and a signed manifest file (ECDSA) including job id, export window, Redwood signer, and timestamp.
   - Optionally, we can notarize the manifest timestamp via a third-party timestamping authority on request.

5) Redaction / PII suppression options:
   - Pre-export redaction: configurable redaction rules (regex, PII classifiers) applied before bundle creation.
   - Deterministic hashing: for identifiers we provide pseudonymization (HMAC-SHA256 with customer-supplied salt) to allow re-linkage if Federated supplies the salt during an investigation.
   - Redaction is logged in the manifest with a redaction_reason and redaction_version to preserve auditability.

6) SLA for a full forensic export:
   - Standard SLA (hosted): 5 business days for up to a 90-day window (typical for up to 1TB of compressed logs).
   - Accelerated SLA (add-on): 48–72 hours for priority customers with reserved extraction capacity.
   - For Dedicated/Private, we can arrange same-day exports depending on local connectivity and permissions.

Attachments: log_extract_playbook_v1.1.pdf (detailed steps & sample manifests), export_manifest_sample.csv (sample rows/fields).

If you want a one-off sample NDJSON for a 7-day window to validate ingestion, we can generate it and ship as a test S3 object. Let me know which fields you need in the manifest; below is a short canonical manifest schema excerpt we use: request_id, timestamp_utc, route, model_version, prompt_truncated_flag, input_token_count, output_token_count, response_crc32, redacted_fields, export_job_id.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the playbook.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: RFI — Log continuity, exportability and delivery SLA clarifications

Looping internal owners. A couple of clarifications before we finalize the playbook to Federated: 

- For Federated's regulatory team, emphasize that model inputs are truncated by default after the policy window but a preservation snapshot can capture full payloads if customer retains on Dedicated/Private.
- Confirm the maximum bundle size we can deliver under the 5-business-day SLA and whether we pro-rate for >1TB. I think we should state a clear threshold (1TB) and say larger exports are scheduled with staged deliveries.
- Security: Ben, can you confirm that the signed manifest uses our ECDSA key and that we can add an optional TSA notarization? Also confirm any constraints on presigned S3 (TTL limits).

We should offer an analyst test export (7-day NDJSON) within 48 hours to help Federated validate parsing. I'll draft a one-sheeter highlighting redaction options and the HMAC re-linking flow.

Thanks — will be ready to send once Ben confirms the manifest signing notes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Brian — following up with a pragmatic delivery plan. Per Marissa & Ben's reviews we've made two clarifications in the attached playbook and are happy to: 

1) Produce a 7-day NDJSON test export within 48 hours so Federated can validate parsing and manifest fields.
2) Standard forensic export for a 90-day window will be delivered via presigned S3 link within 5 business days for bundles <= 1TB; larger bundles will be staged (we'll provide ordered manifests).
3) Manifest signing: confirmed — Redwood signs manifests with our ECDSA key and we can include an optional TSA (third-party timestamp) if Federated requires notarization.
4) Redaction options: we will include a redaction_summary.csv in the bundle that lists which rules were applied and which fields were pseudonymized.

Next steps: please confirm (a) a point of contact for the test export (email to deliver link), and (b) whether Federated will provide a salt for deterministic hashing (if you want re-linkability). Once you confirm, we'll queue the test job and send the S3 link.
